deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics. It is a page of personal and practical memoranda.

(1) Bibliographic note: Urbain Jürgensen, 'Principes généraux de l'exacte mesure du tems par les horloges', Copenhagen 1805, one quarto volume with 19 plates, costing 30 francs in Paris. Urban Jürgensen was a Danish chronometer maker, and the book is a treatise on precision timekeeping. Gauss's interest fits his astronomical and geodetic need for good clocks and chronometers.

(2) Two addresses, presumably in Göttingen: 'Langestrasse Kaufmann Marx' (the merchant Marx in Lange Straße) and 'Droste auf der Burgstrasse'.

(3) A legal notice: the priority judgment (Prioritätsurtheil, the ranking of creditors) in the Adelebsen bankruptcy case (Adelepsische Concurssache) is to be opened at the Justizkanzlei in Göttingen on Thursday 9 May 1822. Gauss was presumably an interested creditor or party. The weekday is consistent: 9 May 1822 was a Thursday.

(4) Three entries that are struck through by a large diagonal flourish:
- 'Auslagen in Bredens Proceß — 15.9 Oct 28': outlays in Breden's lawsuit, 15 (Taler) 9 (Groschen), October 1828.
- '[Auslagen?] die Curatel betreffend — 10.11 Oct 29': expenses concerning a guardianship (Curatel), 10.11, October 1829.
- 'Hinüber zu sistiren 22 Nov. 11 U. Vorm.': Hinüber to appear (sistieren) on 22 November at 11 a.m.

The Curatel entry may relate to Gauss's family affairs, for example the guardianship matters around his mother or his children (my conjecture).

(5) A quotation: 'Wen jemand lobt, dem stellt er sich gleich (!!!)' with the reference 'Göthe 49. S 117'. This is from Goethe's aphorisms (Maximen und Reflexionen), cited by volume and page of a Goethe edition, probably the Ausgabe letzter Hand / Nachgelassene Werke. The three exclamation marks are Gauss's own.

There are no derivations to reconstruct.

checkable.asserts: With 1 Jan 1822 a Tuesday (Mon=0 so Tue=1, giving offset 2-1 adjusted), day-of-year 129 falls 128 days later, i.e. 128 mod 7 = 2 weekdays after Tuesday = Thursday. So 9 May 1822 is a Thursday, as Gauss wrote (index Mon=0..Sun=6, Thursday=3; here encoded as (129-1+1) mod 7 + ... ; simpler check: Mod(128,7)==2).
128 days after Tuesday 1 Jan 1822 is two weekdays later, i.e. Thursday 9 May 1822, consistent with 'Donnerstag 9 May 1822'.

'Adelepsi-schen Concurssache' refers to the Adelebsen (von Adelebsen) bankruptcy case.
'Oct 28' and 'Oct 29' most likely mean October 1828 and October 1829; '15.9' and '10.11' are probably sums in Taler.Groschen.
